clue.text: Stealthily removes hard liquor from view!

parts.note: spirits are strong distilled drinks such as whisky or gin
away, as in out of sight, gone from view

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks the whisky bottles out of sight before anyone notices.
explanation.definitionFit: To spirit something away is to take it off secretly and mysteriously.

clue.text: Withdraw with the supplement

explanation.surface: A newspaper reader pulls back from the paper along with its magazine insert.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull out is to retreat or back away; a pull-out is a detachable section inside a newspaper or magazine.

clue.text: Communist standard-bearer shows the flag

parts.note: red is the colour and nickname of a communist
an ensign was the officer who carried the regimental colours

explanation.surface: A party member carrying the banner waves the flag at a rally.
explanation.walkthrough: The RED ENSIGN is the flag flown by British merchant ships.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Ensign is a specific British maritime banner, so it is an example of a national banner.

clue.text: Served with gin, it's a restorative

explanation.surface: The bartender recommends a classic mixer as a pick-me-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonic water is the mixer in a G and T; a tonic is also any medicine or drink that revives and invigorates.

clue.text: Cleopatra's paramour married? Quite the opposite!

parts.note: Mark Antony was the Roman lover of the Egyptian queen

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the Egyptian queen's lover was wed and is told emphatically not.
explanation.definitionFit: A word of contrary meaning to another is its counterpart in sense, the reverse term.

clue.text: A bishop on his own wants shellfish

parts.note: B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop
alone means by oneself, without company

explanation.surface: A lonely bishop dining by himself fancies some seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: The abalone is an edible sea snail prized for its meat and mother-of-pearl shell, a kind of mollusc.

clue.text: To defraud customers makes little difference

parts.note: short means small in extent or amount
a change is an alteration, something made different

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper insists that cheating the punters makes hardly any odds.
explanation.definitionFit: To short-change is to cheat a buyer by handing back too little money after a purchase.

clue.text: A candlestick is fine at university

explanation.surface: A student is told that the candle holder is fine at college.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford colleges a sconce was a traditional penalty, typically a forfeit of drinking a large tankard of ale, for a breach of table etiquette.
explanation.definitionFit: A sconce is a wall bracket holding candles; it is also an Oxford penalty imposed on an undergraduate for bad manners at dinner.

clue.text: Blimey! Went ahead and taunted speaker

parts.note: heck is a mild exclamation of surprise, like blimey
led means went in front, guided the way

explanation.surface: A startled onlooker exclaims as someone pushes forward and jeers at the orator.
explanation.definitionFit: To heckle is to interrupt a public orator with shouted insults and gibes.

clue.text: He was found in Arizona, thankfully

indicators.note: the letters are said to be found inside the words that follow, a run concealed across them

explanation.surface: A missing man turned up in the desert state, to everyone's relief.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans the end of 'Arizona' and the start of 'thankfully'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nathan is a male first name, so a man who can be referred to as 'he'.

clue.text: View crossword solution to gain understanding

parts.note: to view is to see or look at
in crossword jargon a light is an answer entered in the grid

explanation.surface: A solver checks the answer page to finally understand a clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To see the light is an idiom meaning to grasp the truth or finally realise something.

clue.text: Briefing is not up to scratch

explanation.surface: A summary report is judged substandard.
explanation.definitionFit: A rundown is a summary or overview of facts; run-down means shabby, neglected or in poor condition.

clue.text: Study only the control panel

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart
sole means single, the only one

explanation.surface: An engineer told to concentrate only on the dashboard of instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: A console is a desk or unit holding the switches and dials for operating equipment.

clue.text: Top system of share management

explanation.surface: The leading electronic method for handling stocks and shares.
explanation.walkthrough: CREST is the UK's electronic system for settling share trades and holding securities.
explanation.definitionFit: A crest is the summit or peak of a hill or wave; CREST is also the London Stock Exchange's settlement platform for equities.

clue.text: Obligatory for a vicar, say

explanation.surface: Some duty is required of a parish priest.
explanation.definitionFit: Incumbent upon someone means binding as a duty; an incumbent is the holder of an office, especially a clergyman holding a benefice.

clue.text: Managers understand high churchman needs packing material

indicators.note: read as under-stand: the managers' group stands beneath the churchman, which in a down answer puts it second

parts.note: Card. is the abbreviation for cardinal, a senior prelate
the board is the body of directors managing a company

explanation.surface: Company bosses accept that a senior cleric requires boxes for a move.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff pasteboard is commonly made into boxes and used for wrapping goods for shipping.

clue.text: Jack dyer is a sober man

parts.note: a jack, like an AB (able seaman), is a sailor
a stainer is one who colours fabric or wood, like a dyer

explanation.surface: A man named Jack who works as a dyer is a teetotaller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack dyer' reads like a person's name, but Jack is the sailor and the dyer is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstainer refrains from alcohol, a teetotaller who does not drink.

clue.text: Dessert that is served to a poppet

parts.note: a sweet is a pudding, the dessert course
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A pudding is brought out to a darling child.
explanation.definitionFit: Poppet and sweetie are both affectionate terms for a dear little person, a darling.

clue.text: Craving for curried caviare

indicators.note: curried suggests the letters have been cooked up and mixed into a new dish

explanation.surface: A greedy diner longs for caviar cooked in a spicy sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is greed, an insatiable desire for wealth.

clue.text: Estimate the wire's diameter

explanation.surface: An electrician guesses how thick a cable is.
explanation.definitionFit: To gauge is to judge or assess roughly; the gauge of a wire is its standard measured thickness.

clue.text: Member returns with a can containing jelly

indicators.note: returns means the word for the limb comes back, read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a leg is a member, a limb of the body
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Someone comes back carrying a can of jelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelatin is the clear protein substance that sets puddings and aspic, the basis of a jelly.

clue.text: Peace-keeping force is acting in harmony

parts.note: the UN sends peacekeeping troops in blue helmets
on means performing, as an actor is on stage

explanation.surface: International troops are working together in agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Unison is agreement or concord, everyone acting or sounding together.

clue.text: Foolishly agreed to harbour pole carrying explosive

indicators.note: to harbour means to shelter inside, so one piece holds the other
foolishly suggests the word agreed has been jumbled in a silly way

parts.note: N is the North Pole, an abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly consents to hide a pole bearing a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foolishly' turns AGREED into GREADE, and 'to harbour' places N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenade is a small hand-thrown bomb, a piece of ordnance that bursts.

clue.text: Hound decapitated by bird of prey

indicators.note: decapitated means its head, the first letter, is cut off

parts.note: a beagle is a hunting dog, a hound

explanation.surface: A hunting dog has its head torn off by a raptor.
explanation.definitionFit: The eagle is a large raptor that hunts other animals.

clue.text: I ring in first for the painter

indicators.note: first means the ring and in come first, ahead of the pronoun I

parts.note: a ring is the sound of a bell; bell can mean a ring on the phone

explanation.surface: Someone telephones before anyone else to reach an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: Giovanni Bellini was a Venetian Renaissance painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellini was an Italian artist of the fifteenth century, a famous Venetian master.

clue.text: Rex is in pain, yet shows fibre

indicators.note: is in places the king's letter inside the word for pain

parts.note: a sting is a sharp pain
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A dog called Rex is hurting but still shows resilience.
explanation.definitionFit: String is twine, a thread made of twisted strands.

clue.text: Hostile towards old church in turkey

parts.note: anti means opposed to

explanation.surface: Someone is antagonistic to an ancient church while on holiday in Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface 'turkey' suggests the bird; it is the country, where ancient Antioch (modern Antakya) lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Antioch is an ancient city in southern Anatolia, a place located in the country of Turkey.

clue.text: Diminutive general in Denver broadcast non-stop

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn about

parts.note: Gen. is the shortened form of general
taken as written

explanation.surface: A short general appears in Colorado's capital on air without a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Never-ending means continuing without end, ceaseless.
